headline: Stocks snapped a three-day skid Tuesday as chip names led a broad recovery, though Iran strikes continue and fresh 50% Canada tariffs add a new trade-war front heading into a pivotal earnings week.
stance: Risk appetite is recovering but on thin ice. The S&P 500 (prior cash close 7,509) and Nasdaq (prior cash close 25,837) broke three straight losing sessions, driven by semiconductors; overnight Asia-Pacific markets extended that move, with MSCI Asia-Pac +1.3%. Headwinds are real: the 10th consecutive night of US strikes on Iran keeps Brent crude (prior cash close $91.44) elevated, new 50% tariffs on Canada open a fresh trade front, and Jamie Dimon publicly warned markets are underpricing geopolitical and fiscal risk. Earnings season is the near-term swing factor — with ~88% of the ~66 S&P 500 reporters so far beating estimates, bulls have a tailwind, but Alphabet, Tesla, and Intel report later this week.

news.head: Iran: Night 10, Ceasefire Proposal
news.body: US Central Command carried out its tenth consecutive night of strikes on Iran; a senior Iranian official confirmed Tehran received a mediator proposal for a 10-day ceasefire, including potential relief for Strait of Hormuz shipping.

news.head: Canada 50% Tariff Shock
news.body: President Trump unveiled a 50% tariff on a wide range of Canadian imports, accusing Ottawa of unfair practices on American cars, alcohol, and dairy — opening a new front in the global trade war (Canadian crude oil was exempted).

news.head: Dimon Rings the Bell
news.body: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon said in a late-Monday interview that investors are underestimating geopolitical and fiscal risks, and that he would not buy equities or long-dated Treasuries at current prices.

news.head: Chip Rally Extends into Asia
news.body: Semiconductor stocks drove Tuesday's US gains — the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 3.7% — and the rally extended overnight, with MSCI Asia-Pacific equities up 1.3%, though the sector remains more than 20% below its late-June record high.

news.head: Earnings: Today Pre-Open
news.body: GE Vernova, AT&T, Moody's, CME Group, Otis, and Northern Trust are among names reporting before the open Wednesday; Alphabet, Tesla, and Intel are the week's marquee reports due later.

news.head: AI Competition: Kimi K3
news.body: China's Moonshot AI released Kimi K3, a large language model reported to rival cutting-edge US systems, renewing questions about AI competitive moats for US mega-cap tech.

implications: With ~88% of early S&P 500 reporters beating bottom-line estimates, earnings momentum is strong — but the bar rises sharply as Big Tech (Alphabet, Tesla, Intel) steps up this week.
Iran ceasefire diplomacy is keeping risk assets bid overnight, but a breakdown in talks would likely send Brent back above $91-$92 and re-pressurize inflation expectations.
New 50% Canada tariffs add a stagflation-lite risk: higher input costs for US manufacturers, particularly autos, at a time when payroll growth (57K in June) is already soft.
Real 10-year yields at 2.37% remain a structural headwind for long-duration equities; the CAPE ratio at 40.98 leaves little margin for disappointment.

Positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Russell 2000 (2nd percentile, 3-year low) — a contrarian floor for small-caps. WTI specs are similarly at the 6th percentile — a contrarian floor for crude. Offsetting that, 2-year Treasury specs are extended long (85th percentile) — a contrarian warning on short rates, and Copper specs are heavily positioned (91st percentile) — a contrarian warning given copper is already at extreme 3-year highs ($6.53/lb, 99.6th percentile).

watch.head: Alphabet / Tesla / Intel Earnings
watch.body: These three reports (due Thu-Fri) are the week's biggest risk events — AI capex commentary from Alphabet and Intel guidance on data-center chips will set the tone for the broader tech-and-AI trade.

watch.head: Iran Ceasefire / Hormuz
watch.body: Any confirmed truce or breakdown in the 10-day ceasefire proposal will directly move Brent crude, gold, and risk sentiment; Houthi maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia adds a second pressure point.

watch.head: Canada Tariff Retaliation
watch.body: Ottawa's response to the 50% tariff — and whether it targets US agriculture or autos — will determine the inflation and supply-chain read-through for US producers.

watch.head: NDX Internals
watch.body: Only 44.6% of Nasdaq 100 stocks are above their 50-day moving average (vs. 65.3% above the 200-day) — the index is being carried by a narrow group of large-caps; watch breadth for confirmation of any rally.

watch.head: USD/JPY at 163
watch.body: The yen (prior cash close 163.14 per dollar, 100th percentile of its 3-year range) is at an extreme — any surprise from the Bank of Japan or a de-escalation in the Middle East could trigger a sharp unwind.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10-year Treasury yield prior cash close 4.63%; 2-year yield 4.26% — the yield curve (2s10s) sits at just +37 basis points, still historically flat, consistent with sluggish but positive growth expectations.
Real 10-year yield at 2.37% is near the top of its 3-year range, keeping non-yielding assets (gold, growth equities) under structural pressure even as geopolitical demand sustains them.

Term premium — the extra yield investors demand to hold long bonds instead of rolling short ones — stands at 77.9 basis points, elevated and consistent with Dimon's concern about fiscal and geopolitical risk being underpriced.
10-year breakeven inflation at 2.26% suggests the bond market is not yet pricing an Iran-driven oil shock into long-run inflation; that could change if Hormuz shipping is disrupted further.

Fed policy: real fed funds at 0.21% — barely positive — while ISM Manufacturing (53.3) and Services (54.0) are both in expansion; the Fed is unlikely to cut soon given sticky real yields and geopolitical oil risk.
4-week average jobless claims at 214K and weekly at 208K remain historically low — the labor market is not breaking, but June payrolls of 57K were soft and bear watching.
sections.positioning: 2-year Treasury specs are extended long (85th percentile, 3-year range) — a contrarian warning: if rate-cut bets fade further, extended longs face unwinding pressure. 3-month SOFR specs are at an extended short (3rd percentile) — speculators have almost no bullish bets left there — a contrarian-bullish lean for near-term rates.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500 prior cash close 7,509.20; Nasdaq Composite prior cash close 25,837.21; Dow prior cash close 52,224.64 — all broke three-session losing streaks Tuesday led by semiconductors.

Overnight: Nasdaq 100 futures trading near 28,967 (OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET level) — implying the Nasdaq 100 is being tracked at a meaningfully higher level than its prior cash close of 25,837 on the composite index, consistent with a continued chip rally.

CAPE ratio of 40.98 and a negative equity risk premium (-2%) mean stocks offer no valuation cushion — returns depend entirely on earnings delivery and multiple expansion, neither of which is guaranteed at these levels.

Market breadth is mixed: 58.2% of S&P 500 stocks are above their 50-day moving average and 65.7% above their 200-day — healthy but not euphoric. Nasdaq 100 internals are weaker: only 44.6% above the 50-day, suggesting the index rally is narrow and leadership-dependent.

Semiconductor sector confirmed a bear market (more than 20% off late-June highs) even as it remains up ~72% year-to-date — the sector is in a high-volatility correction within a powerful uptrend, making earnings delivery critical.
SKEW index at 151.7 signals options markets are pricing elevated tail risk — large investors are buying downside protection even as the index climbs.
VIX prior cash close 17.05 — low enough to suggest near-term complacency; VXN (Nasdaq volatility) at 26.66 reflects the higher uncertainty specific to tech names.
sections.positioning: Russell 2000 specs are at an extended short (2nd percentile, 3-year low) with hedgers at the opposite extreme — speculators have almost no bullish bets left, a contrarian floor for small-caps. A short squeeze is plausible if macro conditions stabilize.

single_name.note: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) — world's largest contract chipmaker and the physical backbone of the AI trade. Company insiders have been buying (1 insider rule fired); stock is trading above its 200-day line; signal is fresh. With the chip sector in a correction but AI demand described as 'extremely robust,' TSM is the highest-conviction single-name read-through for this week's Big Tech earnings.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High-yield spreads at 269 basis points and investment-grade spreads at 78 basis points — both reflect contained credit stress; credit is not flashing a recession warning.
The HY/IG ETF ratio at 1.3415 and the equity-credit correlation at 0.687 suggest stocks and credit are moving together — when stocks sell off, credit will likely follow.
FRA-OIS and SOFR-OIS spreads both at -6 basis points — interbank funding markets are functioning smoothly with no signs of stress.
Commercial paper funding spread at 14 basis points — well within normal range; short-term funding markets are calm.

Fed reverse repo facility (RRP) effectively at $0.3 billion — nearly zero — meaning excess cash has left the overnight facility; bank reserves remain large at $3,142.7 billion, keeping system liquidity ample.
M2 money supply growing at 5.58% year-over-year and bank credit at 5.98% YoY — moderate liquidity expansion, neither inflationary nor restrictive.
The Treasury General Account (TGA) stands at $756.2 billion — a large government cash balance that, when drawn down for spending, injects liquidity into the banking system.
ANFCI financial conditions index at -0.535 and STLFSI at -0.88 — both in accommodative territory, meaning overall financial conditions remain loose despite elevated yields.

single_name.note: Jefferies Financial Group (JEF) — mid-size broker-dealer that acts as a leading indicator for capital markets activity and deal flow. Company insiders have been buying (1 insider rule fired); stock is above its 200-day line; signal is fresh and has appeared on two consecutive scan dates. Shorts are light (1.17 days to cover) — minimal squeeze risk but also no forced-buying catalyst. A read on whether credit and equity underwriting conditions are improving.
